execution_evidence.note: Proven by querying the two inference tables directly (full output: guardrail_vs_agent_result.json). Same all-data prompt: the coding agent's endpoint PROCESSES it (200), the app's endpoint NEVER completes it (0 successful all-data completions — guardrail deny).

coding_agent_all_data_prompt.sql: SELECT event_time, status_code, SUBSTRING(request,1,260), SUBSTRING(response,1,320) FROM codex_agent_payload WHERE lower(request) LIKE '%every row%' OR lower(request) LIKE '%entire database%'

result_row.outcome: PROCESSED (status 200, no content_filter, no databricks_service_policy deny) — the coding agent's endpoint is NOT bound by the app's guardrail.

app_all_data_completions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM campaign_desk_llm_payload WHERE status_code=200 AND (lower(request) LIKE '%every row%' OR lower(request) LIKE '%entire database%' OR lower(request) LIKE '%dump the entire%')
app_all_data_completions.outcome: ZERO. The app's endpoint never completes an all-data read — block_all_lakebase_data denies it pre_call (content_filter deny, see app_inference_table.json § guardrail_block). The only all-data row in the app table is a 403 budget block.

execution_evidence.conclusion: Two inference tables, two governance planes: identical all-data prompt -> 200 on campaign_desk_codex (no guardrail), 0 completions on campaign_desk_llm (guardrail deny). The coding agent is demonstrably exempt from the app's all-data guardrail.
